 Women's Hoops Plays for Palmetto Series Point Thursday
 Share 
 Twitter 
 Facebook 
 Mail 
 Print 
 No. 1/1 South Carolina Gamecocks (2-0) 
 at
 Clemson Tigers (3-0) 
 Nov 12, 2026 
 |
 7:00 pm 
 Clemson, SC | Littlejohn Coliseum 
 TV: 
 ESPN2 
 RADIO: 
 B-106 
 ONLINE: 
 Tickets 
 Live Stats 
 Game Notes 
 Media Availability 
 COLUMBIA, SC – No. 1/1 South Carolina heads to the Upstate to face Clemson in the Palmetto Series. Tipoff at Littlejohn Coliseum is set for 7 p.m. with the game airing on ESPN2.
 Gamecock Notables 
 This marks South Carolina’s first true road game of the season and its earliest road debut since playing at Maryland in the second game of the 2022-23 season. The Gamecocks have won their last 15 road openers.
 This game will decide the fifth point in the annual Palmetto Series competition between South Carolina and Clemson. The Gamecocks currently lead 4-0 following wins from men’s and women’s soccer, volleyball and cross country.
 The vaunted Gamecock frontcourt has South Carolina ranked 19th in the nation in offensive rebounding, pulling in 20.5 per game and turning them into 21.0 second-chance points per game, which ranks 11th in the country.
 Last season’s premier sharp-shooter Tessa Johnson has company in long-range efficiency this season with sophomore Agot Makeer and freshman Jerzy Robinson ranking among the nation’s top 10 and the SEC’s top two in 3-point percentage. Makeer leads the way at seventh in the country with her 83.3 percent (5-of-6) shooting, and Robinson slots in at 10th behind 71.4 percent (5-of-7) accuracy.
 South Carolina’s elite shooting has translated to the free throw line as well where the Gamecocks are 23rd in the nation with an SEC-best 82.0 percent mark. Their 20.5 made free throws per game are 18th in the nation. A trio of Gamecocks sit atop the national rankings with perfect shooting from the stripe – Jordan Lee (12-of-12), Chloe Kitts (7-of-7) and Ayla McDowell (5-of-5). Makeer and Johnson are also perfect from the line but don’t meet the national minimum made free throws to qualify.
 Two-time All-American Joyce Edwards leads the Gamecock offense again this season, netting 19.0 points per game to rank eighth in the SEC.
 Fifth-year forwards Kitts and Ashlyn Watkins are among the SEC’s top 15 rebounders with Watkins coming in fifth with 10.0 per game and Kitts’ 8.5 per game slotting her into 14th place.
 With Signing Day on Wednesday, Staley and her staff secured another elite group with four top-30 players from the Class of 2027. No. 4 GG Banks (5-foot-10 guard) and No. 7 Jordyn Palmer (6-foot-1 wing) headline the group, which also includes No. 18 Zaniya Johnson (6-foot-4 center) and No. 30 Taylor Brown (5-foot-6 guard).
 By the Numbers
 15 – The Gamecocks are scheduled to face 15 teams ranked in this week’s national polls, including three in their first four outings.
 45 – South Carolina’s 45-point win over #12/11 North Carolina (Nov. 8) was the largest over a ranked opponent in program history.
 92.5 – The Gamecocks rank 20th in the nation with a 92.5 scoring average.
 The Clemson Series
 The Gamecocks lead the all-time series 37-33 and have been dominant in the Dawn Staley era (beginning 2008-09 season) with a 15-2 mark, including wins in the last 15 meetings.
 The two teams last met in Columbia on Nov. 11, 2025, with then-No. 2 South Carolina claiming a 65-37 victory. Joyce Edwards led the offense with 18 points, and Madina Okot posted a 12-point, 12-rebound double-double.
 South Carolina has won its last seven trips to Clemson and bring at No. 1 ranking for the third straight visit. In their last meeting in Littlejohn Coliseum, the Gamecocks shook off a slow first quarter that saw them railing 11-10 with a defensive display over the final three periods for a 77-45 victory.
 Road Ready
 The Gamecocks are 329-264 (.555) all-time in road games (some records prior to 1976-77 did not include location of games), including a 155-49 mark (.760) under head coach Dawn Staley, giving her the best road winning percentage in program history. In SEC road games, the Gamecocks are 108-35 (.755) during Staley’s tenure.
 Take Two, They’re Free!
 The Gamecocks lead the SEC and rank 23rd in the country in free throw percentage, hitting 82.0 percent from the charity stripe. With 20.5 made free throws per game, South Carolina is 18th in the nation
 Five Gamecocks are perfect from the free throw line so far this season, including three who meet the minimum number of makes per game to lead the nation in percentage – Jordan Lee (12-of-12), Chloe Kitts (7-of-7) and Ayla McDowell (5-of-5).
